key_insight: PathScale-R1 improves pathological image reasoning by training models to use evidence across multiple magnification scales instead of relying on single-scale shortcuts.
clinical_relevance: This could help build more reliable AI tools for pathology interpretation by better matching the multi-scale way pathologists assess tissue and cells.
method: Built PathScale-VQA, a cross-scale pathology VQA benchmark with shortcut-resistant question design.
Used adversarial text-only screening for semantic questions and structure-controlled distractor sampling for visual grounding questions.
Optimized PathScale-R1 with difficulty-driven reasoning distillation and reinforcement learning using a scale-aware reasoning reward.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 10,373 multiple-choice questions grounded in 1,368 diagnostic paths across multiple magnification levels, and the paper reports state-of-the-art performance plus transfer to single-scale pathology VQA.
watch_item: Performance may depend on benchmark design and the quality of cross-scale supervision, so real-world robustness should still be validated on external pathology data.
paper_title: PathScale-R1: Cross-scale Reasoning for Pathological Image Analysis
